Dear Wanderer, as I write, I picture your face.
Some days ago, this old man accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the local school. There, I saw the children sitting upright, heads buried in books, so engrossed they didn’t even notice our approach.
Curious, I wondered what marvelous texts could captivate these usually restless youngsters. Upon asking, I learned they were reading books you had gifted them not long ago.
When I inquired what made these books so special, the children eagerly chimed in, revealing that you had thoughtfully selected different books for each child. Hearing that I knew you, they begged me to convey their gratitude.
Yet, when pressed to express their thanks aloud, they grew shy and tongue-tied. So, I suggested they put their thoughts into writing, which I’ve enclosed here—unread, I assure you!
Oh, and they also entrusted me with a few drawings, inspired by the books they read. They insisted you, with your discerning eye, would appreciate their masterpieces.
Ha Ha, it seems for any future tasks involving children, you’re the one to call.
